reason: E1 directly states that IrOsPtPdRhRu catalyzes a 12-electron ethanol oxidation process, supporting the baseline claim. E2 demonstrates that alloying creates isolated Pt/Pd sites with charge transfer that enhances catalytic performance, supporting the ligand-effect mechanism. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that disrupting random mixing reduces selectivity or that the specific synergy governs ethanol oxidation selectivity; these mechanistic links are hypothesized without direct prior support.
premises: Random atomic mixing in HEAs creates isolated Pt/Pd sites with tuned electronic environments via ligand effects from neighboring metals.
This electronic tuning optimizes adsorption energies of ethanol and intermediates, enabling complete 12-electron oxidation.
Disrupting random mixing (e.g., by annealing) reduces ligand effects, shifting selectivity toward less complete oxidation.
The cited IrOsPtPdRhRu HEA catalyzes a 12-electron ethanol oxidation process, unlike single metals.
In PtPdCoCuNi HEA, charge transfer to Pt/Pd enhances catalytic performance via isolated sites.
